scenes.heading: Data Warehouse Basics
scenes.subheading: A central home for analytical data
scenes.narration: A data warehouse is a central repository that stores integrated, historical data optimized for analysis and reporting.

scenes.heading: What defines a warehouse
bullets: Serves as the single source of truth
scenes.narration: A warehouse integrates data from many source systems into one consistent place. It stores cleaned, modeled, and historical data rather than raw operational records. It is optimized for large analytical queries rather than fast individual writes. And it serves as the single source of truth that everyone in the business can trust.

scenes.heading: How data reaches the warehouse
scenes.narration: Data is extracted from operational sources across the business. It is transformed and cleaned into a consistent, modeled shape. It is then loaded into the warehouse, where analysts run reports and dashboards against a single trusted dataset.

scenes.heading: Operational database vs warehouse
scenes.narration: An operational database holds current data and is tuned for the fast writes that keep an application running. A warehouse holds integrated historical data and is tuned for the heavy reads that power analysis. Separating them keeps analytics from ever slowing down the live systems.

scenes.text: A data warehouse is the integrated, historical single source of truth built for analysis.
scenes.narration: The main idea is that a data warehouse serves as an integrated, historical single source of truth purpose-built for analysis and reporting.
